In addition, relocatees receive an across-the-board dislocation allowance of $200. Dislocated parties have the alternative of receiving reimbursement for the actual reasonable moving expenses.
The second type of payment is a rental replacement housing payment. Tenants or homeowners who have lived in the area for not less than three months, who cannot obtain comparable decent, safe and sanitary housing at rent levels equal to their previous rent, or whose relocation rent would exceed 25 percent of their income, are eligible for a rental housing payment to make up the difference in this higher rent. This payment is made only for four years and cannot exceed $83.33 per month toward the reduction of the monthly rental cost of relocatees.
Tenants and short-term homeowners can use the not-to-exceed $4,000 rent replacementpayment toward a down payment for a home if they wish to purchase rather than rent. Homeowners of more than three months, but less than six months, and renters of three months or more, are eligible for this down payment subsidy.
The third type of payment available is a replacement housing payment for homeowners. Displaced owner-occupants who have lived in the area for six months or longer are entitled to replacement housing payments up to, but not to exceed, $15,000. These payments will pay for the additional costs of buying and paying fora comparable decent, safe and sanitary home. This payment can cover the higher interest rates and costs of less favorable financing, and incidental payments such as legal fees, FHA or VA appraisal fees, and other incidental costs involved in purchasing a home.
